correctness.rationale: Reconstructed all seven source files, canonical Git tree and complete proof. Each group endomorphism has the unique mixed-modulus matrix T=((u,v),(p^(b-a)w,z)); squaring yields four necessary and sufficient congruences with the proper two row moduli. For a=1, u=0 and the valuation of z² distinguishes the t=vw=0 fiber from the possible odd-b nonzero t; resulting 2p−1 and (p−1)² terms give both formulas. For a=2, the exact Z/p² product-fiber count (zero p(3p−2), valuation-one 2p(p−1), unit p(p−1)) and α=u/p split yield all b≥5 cases. Separately reconstructed b=3 and b=4 where z need not vanish mod p² and α can be forced to −z/p; the algebra gives the advertised boundary expressions. All p, including 2, and every b>a are covered; no assertion for a≥3. Direct generator-image enumeration independently matches 40 bounded (p,a,b) instances, all 87 residue product fibers for p=2,3,5,7 and five symbolic simplifications. Universal truth follows from the p-adic case analysis, not these finite checks.

value.rationale: The cardinality of {T∈End(G):Im T⊆Ker T} is a natural invariant measuring two-step collapse in a finite abelian group, important for studying the nonunit endomorphism monoid. Its complete value for the first two unequal shorter cyclic exponents, for all primes and arbitrarily large longer exponent, is not a rename of an automorphism count or a known table. The nontrivial new feature at a=2 is the p² product-fiber stratification and low-boundary anomaly; the parity-sensitive Q(a,b+2)=pQ(a,b) is a uniform structural law. The exact formulas stand as a useful count without claiming a general a≥3 classification or downstream theorem.
